cards.back: A customer who is either (1) age 65 or older, OR (2) age 18 or older and reasonably believed by the member to have a mental or physical impairment that renders the individual unable to protect his or her own interests.

cards.front: Financial exploitation of a specified adult
cards.back: The wrongful or unauthorized taking, withholding, appropriation, or use of a specified adult's funds or securities; OR any act/omission to obtain control—through deception, intimidation, or undue influence—over the specified adult's money, assets, or property, including through a power of attorney, guardianship, or other authority.

cards.front: When must a member firm make reasonable efforts to obtain the name and contact information of a trusted contact person?
cards.back: When opening a new customer account or when updating account information for an existing account. The firm is not prohibited from opening the account if the customer refuses, provided reasonable efforts were made.

cards.front: What is the purpose of a trusted contact person?
cards.back: To serve as a resource for the member firm in administering the customer's account, protecting assets, and responding to possible financial exploitation. The firm may contact the trusted contact to confirm the customer's contact info, health status, identity of legal guardian/trustee/POA, or to discuss suspected exploitation.

cards.front: Under FINRA Rule 2165, how long may a member firm place a temporary hold on a disbursement or transaction from a specified adult's account?
cards.back: Initially up to 15 business days. The firm may internally extend the hold an additional 10 business days (25 total). If the matter has been reported to a state regulator, agency, or court, the hold may be extended an additional 30 business days, for up to 55 business days total.

cards.front: What may a temporary hold under FINRA Rule 2165 be placed on?
cards.back: Both disbursements of funds/securities AND securities transactions in the account of a specified adult, when the firm reasonably believes financial exploitation has occurred, is occurring, has been attempted, or will be attempted.

cards.front: When a member firm places a temporary hold under Rule 2165, what notification and review obligations are triggered?
cards.back: The firm must (1) immediately begin an internal review of the facts and circumstances, and (2) provide notification of the hold and the reason no later than 2 business days after initiation to the trusted contact person and all parties authorized to transact business in the account—unless that person is unavailable or reasonably believed to be the perpetrator.

cards.front: FINRA Rule 3241 (registered person named as customer beneficiary/fiduciary)
cards.back: Before being named as a beneficiary, executor, trustee, or holder of power of attorney for a customer who is NOT an immediate family member, a registered person must provide written notice to the firm and receive the firm's written approval. Effective 2/15/2021.

Any use of a customer's funds or securities in a way other than that intended by the customer. All such uses are prohibited. Common example: borrowing or lending between a representative and a customer without proper firm authorization.

cards.front: Under what five circumstances may FINRA's Conduct Rules permit a registered representative to borrow from or lend to a customer (assuming the firm has written procedures allowing it)?
cards.back: (1) Immediate family member (no notice or approval needed); (2) Customer is in the business of lending money, e.g., a bank (no approval needed); (3) Both customer and RR are registered persons at the same firm (firm approval required); (4) Personal relationship outside the broker-customer relationship (firm approval required); (5) Business relationship outside the broker-customer relationship (firm approval required).

cards.front: Seabird Securities has NO written firm policies regarding borrowing/lending arrangements between associated persons and customers. Under which circumstance may an RR borrow from a customer?
cards.back: Under no circumstance. If the firm does not have written procedures permitting such arrangements, no borrowing or lending between RRs and customers is allowed—even from family members.

cards.front: May a BD, investment adviser, or RR guarantee a customer against a loss or guarantee a gain?
cards.back: No. All guarantees—or anything intended to convey a guarantee—are strictly prohibited.

cards.front: Under what conditions may an RR share in profits and losses of a customer's account?
cards.back: Only in a joint account that has received the firm's prior written approval, and the RR may share only in direct proportion to his financial contribution to the account. Contribution is measured in dollars, not knowledge or expertise. Firms themselves may not have joint accounts with customers.

cards.front: What is the exception to the proportionate sharing rule for joint accounts?
cards.back: Sharing of profits and losses need not be directly proportionate when the joint account is with an immediate family member (parents, in-laws, spouses, children, and anyone to whom the RR contributes financial support, including those living in the same residence).

cards.front: List examples of red flags for improper use of customer funds that BDs are expected to detect.
cards.back: Suspicious transfers and disbursements in customer accounts; activity in the account of a deceased person; excessive customer complaints; and exception reports showing discrepancies such as conflicting addresses, a street address not matching a city/ZIP, or a telephone area code not matching the address provided.

cards.front: What activities are permitted for nonregistered (unlicensed) employees of a broker-dealer?
cards.back: Responding to general, noninvestment questions (hours, taking messages, directions); providing literature on request; setting appointments; inviting prospects to seminars; and handling customer money and securities (with fingerprinting required for those handling assets). They may NOT engage in investment banking or securities business such as opening accounts or soliciting trades.

cards.front: After passing the SIE exam but before passing a top-off (representative-level) exam, what activities may a person perform?
cards.back: Only those permitted to a nonregistered/unlicensed person. The individual is not yet registered. Performing the functions of a registered representative before licensing can result in being barred from the industry.

cards.front: A nonregistered receptionist at a BD opens all incoming mail and forwards it to various employees of the firm. Must this person be (a) fingerprinted and (b) registered with FINRA?
cards.back: (a) Yes — fingerprinting is required because the receptionist handles customer assets (mail may contain checks/securities). (b) No — registration with FINRA is not required, because the receptionist does not engage in securities business.

cards.front: Which of these customers is of special concern for potential financial exploitation under FINRA rules: a 70-year-old client, a 60-year-old, a 30-year-old known to be irresponsible, or a 55-year-old going through a midlife crisis?
cards.back: The 70-year-old. FINRA's specified-adult protections apply to customers age 65 or older, or age 18+ with a mental/physical impairment rendering them unable to protect their own interests. Irresponsibility or a midlife crisis does not qualify.
